checks.title: Set up naming and PostScript names
checks.info:
Fill in the family name, style names and PostScript names in Font Info. Style names use plain title case (Bold Italic, not bold-italic), PostScript names carry no spaces or special characters, and family plus style should stay well under 63 characters.

Names are what operating systems and apps use to group and find the family, so mistakes here surface everywhere at once. The Glyphs naming tutorial covers how each name type should be written.

checks.title: Set up style linking
checks.info:
In Font Info > Exports, link the Bold, Italic and Bold Italic instances to their base style. Other styles stay unlinked unless there is a reason.

Style linking is what makes the Bold and Italic buttons in Word or InDesign pick the right file. Whether it behaves in real apps is a separate check under Final QA.

checks.title: Place the masters correctly in the designspace
checks.info:
Give every master its intended axis coordinates in Font Info > Masters, and keep all instances inside the range the masters span.

Two masters at the same location, or an axis with masters at only one position, cannot interpolate. Instances outside the range have to be extrapolated, which distorts shapes.

checks.title: Confirm the default master is the intended style
checks.info:
Check which master is the origin of the variable font — the Variable Font Origin custom parameter, or the first master when none is set.

The origin is what apps show before any axis is touched, and what a fallback renderer uses. It should be the style the family is meant to lead with.

checks.title: Add the 'Use Typo Metrics' parameter
checks.info:
Add Use Typo Metrics in Font Info > Font, and make sure the typo metrics themselves are filled in.

With this set (fsSelection bit 7), apps use the typo values for line spacing instead of the win values, which is the consistent choice across platforms and a Google Fonts requirement.

checks.title: Complete the version number and font info
checks.info:
Set a release version number and fill in designer, manufacturer, copyright and license in Font Info.

These fields travel inside every exported file and show up in font managers, licensing tools and Get Info panels. Empty ones look unfinished and make the font hard to trace.

checks.title: Keep PostScript names within the length limits
checks.info:
Check that the PostScript name of every exporting instance stays at or under 63 characters.

Longer names break in older environments and some PDF workflows; under 31 characters is safer still if the family has to work in legacy applications.

checks.title: Match weight and width names to their classes
checks.info:
Check that each instance's weight class and width class agree with its style name — Light should carry 300, Condensed should carry 3.

Apps sort and substitute styles by these numbers, not by the name. A mismatch puts styles in the wrong order in menus, or makes two styles look identical to the system.

checks.title: Keep variable font names apart from the statics
checks.info:
When statics and a variable font ship from the same file, give the variable font its own family name with the Variable Font Family Name parameter.

Installing both under one family name makes them collide: the operating system picks one and quietly ignores the other, which is hard to diagnose later.

checks.title: Set the Vendor ID
checks.info:
Add the vendorID custom parameter in Font Info > Font. It must be exactly four ASCII characters.

The vendor ID identifies the foundry in the OS/2 table and appears in font managers. Registering it with Microsoft keeps it unique.

checks.title: Check the copyright years and ownership
checks.info:
Read the copyright string in Font Info: correct years, correct owner, consistent with the license text.

This is the legal notice that ships inside every file. A stale year or a name carried over from another project is easy to miss and awkward to correct after release.

checks.title: Decide the PANOSE values deliberately
checks.info:
Leave PANOSE unset, which means all zeros ('any'), or set values that genuinely describe the design.

All zeros is the safe neutral. Values left over from another project mislead the systems that use PANOSE for font matching and substitution.

checks.title: Give every glyph its expected Unicode value
checks.info:
Check that exporting glyphs which should carry a codepoint actually have one.

Without a Unicode value a glyph cannot be typed, copied or found by a screen reader — it is only reachable through a feature. Glyphs assigns most codepoints automatically from the glyph name.

checks.title: Remove duplicate Unicode values
checks.info:
Check that no two exporting glyphs claim the same codepoint.

The cmap table maps each codepoint to exactly one glyph, so a duplicate silently makes one of the two unreachable — usually the one nobody tests.

checks.title: Follow the Google Fonts vertical metrics strategy
checks.info:
If the project targets Google Fonts, or simply wants one documented strategy, set typo, hhea and win metrics in the specific relationship the Google Fonts guide describes, including a typo line gap of zero.

Following one strategy consistently is what makes line spacing identical across macOS, Windows and browsers. Fontspector verifies the result on the compiled binary.

checks.title: Keep uppercase diacritics below the clipping boundary
checks.info:
Check that the tallest glyphs — uppercase diacritics in particular — stay inside the win metrics in every master.

Windows applications clip anything above winAscent or below winDescent. The tops of accented capitals are usually the first thing to disappear.

checks.title: Keep vertical metrics identical across masters
checks.info:
Check that every master carries the same vertical metric values.

Metrics that differ between masters make line spacing jump when the weight changes, and produce inconsistent interpolated instances.

checks.title: Keep line spacing consistent across the family
checks.info:
Compare the vertical metrics of every style — masters, instance overrides, and the other files of the family if they are open.

Setting a paragraph in Regular and switching it to Italic should not change the leading. Roman and italic files drifting apart is the classic cause.

checks.title: Check that shapes match the alignment zones
checks.info:
Compare overshoots of round shapes against the zones in Font Info > Masters: overshoots inside the zone, flat shapes on the flat edge.

Zones that miss the actual shapes are worse than no zones, because hinting then aligns the wrong outlines. This stays a manual read: on real fonts, near-misses are as often deliberate as accidental.

checks.title: Check that stem thickness is consistent
checks.info:
Compare vertical stems against each other, and horizontals against each other, across the alphabet and across masters.

Inconsistent stems read as uneven colour in text. The Stem Thickness reporter measures stems live under the cursor; the judgement stays human, since many designs vary stems on purpose.

checks.title: Check for almost-straight segments
checks.info:
Look for curve segments that are nearly but not exactly straight, and decide whether they should be true straights.

They are usually drawing accidents, and they show up as subtle wobble at large sizes. Red Arrow flags them directly in the edit view.

checks.title: Check for kinks in the outlines
checks.info:
Look for smooth connections that bend where they should stay smooth, especially in interpolated instances.

A kink can be invisible in the masters and obvious halfway between them. Kink Finder reports them across the whole designspace.

checks.title: Place points at the extremes
checks.info:
Check that every curve has nodes at its topmost, bottommost, leftmost and rightmost points.

Missing extremes hurt rendering at small sizes, break hinting, and make interpolation unpredictable. Red Arrow flags them in the edit view.

checks.title: Check for zero handles
checks.info:
Look for offcurve points that sit exactly on their oncurve point — handles retracted to zero length.

They break rendering in some engines and behave unpredictably in interpolation. Red Arrow flags them in the edit view.

checks.title: Check that terminals are consistent
checks.info:
Compare stroke endings across the font: angle, weight and shape should follow one logic.

Terminals are among the strongest signals of a family's character, so an inconsistent one reads as a mistake rather than a variation.

checks.title: Check that diagonals are consistent
checks.info:
Compare the diagonal strokes of v, w, x, y, k and their relatives for weight and angle.

Diagonals need optical correction to look as heavy as vertical stems, and that correction has to be applied consistently or the letters fall out of colour.

checks.title: Check that path directions are correct
checks.info:
Check that outer contours and counters run in the correct directions.

Wrong directions make counters fill in. Static exports correct this automatically when overlaps are removed, so it matters most for variable fonts, where nothing fixes it at export.

checks.title: Draw a custom .notdef
checks.info:
Draw a .notdef glyph in every master rather than leaving it to the automatic fallback.

.notdef is what readers see when a character is missing from the font. Glyphs generates a plain box at export; a custom one matches the design and signals that the gap is intentional.

checks.title: Check that the space has an appropriate width
checks.info:
Test the space in running text at several weights, and check that the no-break space matches it.

The space sets the rhythm of every line. Too narrow and words run together, too wide and the text opens up into holes — a judgement only reading can settle.

checks.title: Add the space characters the font needs
checks.info:
Check for the standard set: no-break space, figure space, thin space, hair space, em and en space, punctuation space, zero-width space.

Layout applications and web text rely on these for fixed spacing. Build Space Glyphs adds them with correct, metrics-keyed widths.

checks.title: Remove empty exporting glyphs
checks.info:
Check for glyphs set to export that have no paths, no components and no width.

They are almost always accidents — a glyph added and never drawn. In the font they become invisible zero-width characters that break text unpredictably.

checks.title: Keep brace layers inside the designspace
checks.info:
Check that every brace layer's coordinates fall inside the range the masters span.

A brace layer outside that range never activates: it silently does nothing at export, and the substitution it was drawn for simply never happens.

checks.title: Check for nested and flipped components
checks.info:
Look for components built from other composites, and for components mirrored by a negative scale.

Both export in unpredictable ways and can break interpolation. Component Problem Finder reports these along with other component trouble.

checks.title: Check that diacritics align on their base shapes
checks.info:
Read accented letters in a text tab across all masters, watching how marks sit over their bases.

Anchors place marks mechanically, but optical centring is a judgement — a mark centred on the bounding box often looks wrong on a diagonal or asymmetric letter.

checks.title: Check that anchors are consistent
checks.info:
Check that base letters carry the anchors their marks attach to, and that marks carry the matching underscore anchors.

Anchors drive both automatic composite alignment and the mark features. A missing one means a diacritic lands in the wrong place, or the feature silently skips that letter.

checks.title: Set up the ligature carets
checks.info:
Add caret anchors to every ligature produced by liga, dlig, rlig, clig or hlig — one fewer than the number of parts.

Carets tell text editors where the cursor may fall inside a ligature. Without them, selecting or stepping through a word jumps across the whole ligature at once.

checks.title: Bring the metrics keys back in sync
checks.info:
Check for layers whose sidebearings no longer match their metrics keys — the ones Glyphs shows in red.

An out-of-sync key means the sidebearing was edited by hand after the key was set, so the relationship the key describes is no longer true and later changes will not propagate.

checks.title: Check that no characters are touching
checks.info:
Look for glyph pairs whose outlines touch or overlap once kerning is applied.

Touching letters read as a broken font more than any other spacing fault. Touché scans the whole font for collisions and lists the pairs.

checks.title: Check kerning against the brace and bracket layers
checks.info:
Check the glyphs with alternate layers at the points where those layers switch in.

Kerning is set on the default outlines, but a bracket layer can change the shape entirely — so a pair that fits in the Regular may collide once the alternate takes over.

checks.title: Remove tiny kerning pairs
checks.info:
Look through the kerning for pairs below roughly 5 units and consider deleting them.

A correction that small is invisible at text sizes, but it still costs file size and clutters the kerning when it is reviewed later.

checks.title: Check for overkerns
checks.info:
Look for pairs kerned by more than a sensible share of the glyph widths.

An extreme value is usually a typo or a leftover experiment rather than a decision, and it stands out immediately in text. New Tab with Overkerned Pairs collects them in one tab.

checks.title: Consider whether extension kerning is needed
checks.info:
Decide how far the kerning should reach beyond the core alphabet — punctuation, figures, brackets, quotes, and the classes they belong to.

Most spacing faults readers notice sit at these boundaries rather than between two letters. How far to take it depends on what the family is for.

checks.title: Name the stylistic sets
checks.info:
Give every ssXX feature a readable name in Font Info > Features.

Apps show that name in their stylistic set menu. Without one, the menu offers 'ss03' and nobody can tell what it does.

checks.title: Extend the stylistic sets to related glyphs
checks.info:
Check that composites and diacritics built from a glyph with a stylistic variant have their own variant too.

If a.ss01 exists but aacute.ss01 does not, turning the feature on changes some letters and leaves the accented ones behind — visible immediately in any language that uses them.

checks.title: Cover all uppercase with small caps
checks.info:
Check that every uppercase letter has a small cap counterpart.

A missing one falls back to the full capital, which towers over its neighbours in small cap settings and is impossible to miss once noticed.

checks.title: Give all tabular glyphs the same width
checks.info:
Check that every glyph with a tabular suffix shares one width with the others in its group, in every master.

Figures that do not line up in columns defeat the purpose of tabular figures. Groups are compared separately, so .tf and .tf.sc each keep their own width.

checks.title: Make the math symbols tabular
checks.info:
Check that plus, minus, equals, multiply, divide and their relatives share the tabular width.

Math symbols sit inside columns of figures, so a symbol of a different width breaks the alignment the tabular figures were made for. Tabular Checker reports every glyph that differs.

checks.title: Check the fraction numerators, denominators and slash
checks.info:
Read the precomposed fractions and the frac feature: numerator and denominator alignment, and how the fraction slash spaces against them.

Fractions are built from parts that were designed separately, so they need looking at as a whole before they read as one character.

checks.title: Compile the feature code without errors
checks.info:
Compile the OpenType features and read any errors reported in features, prefixes or classes.

Hand-written code can break long before anyone notices, and a broken feature usually fails silently — it simply never applies.

checks.title: Confirm the intended language coverage
checks.info:
Check which languages the character set actually supports, against the list the project promised.

Intent and reality drift apart easily: one missing accented letter drops a whole language. Hyperglot checks a character set against its language database.

checks.title: Test style linking in real applications
checks.info:
Install a test export and try the Bold and Italic buttons in Word, the style menus in Adobe apps, and the macOS font pickers.

Style linking is defined in the file but interpreted by each application, so the only proof that it works is watching it work.

checks.title: Test real exports in InDesign and a browser
checks.info:
Export the OTF, TTF and variable versions and open them in InDesign and a browser before release.

This catches the class of problems no source-level check can see — compilation faults, feature failures, rendering surprises — while there is still time to fix them.

checks.title: Test the WOFF files in the relevant browsers
checks.info:
Load the webfont exports in the browsers the project cares about and read real text.

Browsers differ in how they render, space and apply features, and webfont-specific problems only appear once the file is served as a webfont.

checks.title: Run the files through Fontspector
checks.info:
Check the compiled binaries with Fontspector before release.

It inspects the exported tables directly, which is the layer this checklist cannot reach: source files can be perfect while the binary still fails a specification check.
